segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And they went out to sport in horse races.
Then, in the fury of the chase, he fell from his horse and died;
and their joy was turned into mourning.
Then the people of Melitene set up in his place Afridun, his younger brother,
and they gave him his brother's wife, though she was unwilling.
Then Qilij Arslan, the Sultan of Iconium, gathered an army and came against Melitene,
and he was not able to subdue it;
but he took the people of the country captive,
and went back to Caesarea.
Then Nur al-Din, the lord of Mardin, the lord of Hisn Ziyad, the Armenians of Cilicia, and the son of Danishmend, the lord of Sebastia, made an alliance (or: made peace),
and they all assembled in Sebastia to wage war with Qilij Arslan.
And they advanced as far as the gate {OCR?} of Caesarea.
Qilij Arslan, however, did not come out to fight,
but sought peace,
and he returned the people whom he had taken captive from Melitene.
And when they demanded of him his four nephews,
who were imprisoned with him,
he committed an outrage:
he slaughtered one of them, roasted him, placed him on a platter,
and sent him to his father.
And he swore that if they asked further for the others,
he would do the same to the three of them as well.
And so they left him and went away.
And in that same year,
which is the year 1482 [of the Greeks],
566 of the Arabs,
Qilij Arslan took control of all the lands of the sons of Danishmend.
And in that same year, when Nur al-Din heard
that his brother Qutb al-Din had died,
and that his son Sayf al-Din had succeeded as king,
and that 'Abd al-Masih was administering the kingdom of Mosul as he pleased,
and making the yoke heavy upon the people,
he was stirred in his spirit and said:
"Is it right for me to direct the affairs of my brother's sons and their kingdom,
or for 'Abd al-Masih?"
And he set out from Aleppo, encamped against Callinicus, and took it;
and he also took control over all of Khabur,
and he also established his rule over Nisibis.
And Muhammad, the son of Qara Arslan, the lord of the Fortress (Hisn), came to him.
And he came and attacked Sinjar and took it,
and he placed in it 'Imad al-Din, his nephew.
And from there he came to the city of Balad and crossed the Tigris,
and went and encamped on the eastern side of Mosul,
that is to say, in the region of Nineveh.
And on the very day that he arrived,
a marvel occurred:
for one of the great towers of Mosul
collapsed of its own accord.
